entity1.name: Black Holes
entity1.description: Regions in space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape, formed by the collapse of massive stars.;;;Regions in space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from them.;;;A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from it.;;;A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, including light, can escape from it.;;;Regions in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that not even light can escape from them.;;;A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that not even light can escape it.;;;A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that not even light can escape.;;;A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that not even light can escape from it, formed by the collapse of massive stars.;;;Regions in space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.;;;Regions in space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape, formed from the collapse of massive stars.;;;A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that not even light can escape from it.;;;Regions in space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape, often associated with various mysteries in physics.;;;Regions in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from them.;;;Regions in space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape, formed from the remnants of massive stars after they collapse.

entity2.name: cosmic entities
entity2.description: Mysterious celestial objects in space, often referring to phenomena like black holes or other massive gravitational structures.

entity3.name: astronomers
entity3.description: Scientists who study celestial objects, space, and the universe as a whole.

entity4.name: physicists
entity4.description: Scientists who study the fundamental properties and behavior of matter and energy, including phenomena in space.

entity8.name: Supernova explosion
entity8.description: A powerful and luminous stellar explosion that occurs during the last evolutionary stages of a massive star.

entity9.name: star
entity9.description: A massive, luminous sphere of plasma held together by gravity, which undergoes nuclear fusion in its core.

entity11.name: singularity
entity11.description: A point at the center of a black hole where density is infinite and volume is zero, according to general relativity.;;;A point of infinite density at the center of a black hole, where the laws of physics as we know them break down.;;;A point at the center of a black hole where matter is thought to be infinitely dense and spacetime curvature becomes infinite.;;;A point in spacetime where the density and curvature become infinite, and the known laws of physics no longer apply.

entity13.name: event horizon
entity13.description: The boundary surrounding a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape its gravitational pull.;;;The radius at which the escape velocity from a black hole equals the speed of light, marking the boundary of the event horizon.;;;The boundary surrounding a black hole beyond which events cannot affect an outside observer; it marks the point of no return for matter and light.;;;The boundary surrounding a black hole beyond which events cannot affect an outside observer.

entity17.name: Gravitational pull
entity17.description: The force exerted by a massive object that attracts other objects towards it.

entity18.name: Spacetime
entity18.description: A four-dimensional continuum combining the three dimensions of space with the dimension of time, as described in the theory of relativity.;;;A mathematical model that combines the three dimensions of space and the one dimension of time into a single four-dimensional continuum.

entity19.name: gravitational time dilation
entity19.description: A phenomenon in physics where time passes slower in stronger gravitational fields, such as near a black hole.

entity23.name: Speed of light
entity23.description: The maximum speed at which all energy, matter, and information in the universe can travel, approximately 299,792,458 meters per second.

entity25.name: light
entity25.description: Electromagnetic radiation that is visible to the human eye and can travel through space.

entity26.name: scientists
entity26.description: Individuals who study and conduct research in various scientific fields, including astronomy and physics.;;;Researchers or experts in a scientific field who are conducting studies or making speculations.

entity28.name: Theoretical physics
entity28.description: A branch of physics that employs mathematical models and abstractions of physical objects and systems to rationalize, explain, and predict natural phenomena.

entity29.name: Holographic principle
entity29.description: A principle in theoretical physics suggesting that the information within a region of space can be described by the information on the boundary of that region.;;;A theoretical principle in physics that suggests all the information contained within a volume of space can be represented as a theory on the boundary of that space, such as the event horizon of a black hole.

entity30.name: Information paradox
entity30.description: A paradox in theoretical physics related to the apparent loss of information in black holes, challenging the principles of quantum mechanics.;;;A theoretical problem in physics concerning the fate of information that enters a black hole and whether it is permanently lost, challenging the principles of quantum mechanics and general relativity.;;;A theoretical problem in physics concerning the apparent loss of information about matter that falls into a black hole, conflicting with the principles of quantum mechanics.

entity34.name: information
entity34.description: Data or content that can be stored, processed, and communicated, often discussed in the context of physics and how it relates to the universe and black holes.

entity35.name: universe
entity35.description: The totality of all space, time, matter, energy, and laws, encompassing everything that exists.;;;The totality of all space, time, matter, energy, and laws that exist, including galaxies, stars, and other celestial phenomena.

entity40.name: fundamental laws of physics
entity40.description: The basic principles that govern the behavior of the physical universe, such as the laws of motion, gravity, and thermodynamics.

entity42.name: General relativity
entity42.description: A theory of gravitation developed by Albert Einstein, describing gravity as a geometric property of space and time.;;;A theory of gravitation that describes the gravitational force as a curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

entity43.name: Quantum mechanics
entity43.description: A fundamental theory in physics that describes the physical properties of nature at the scale of atoms and subatomic particles.

entity44.name: String theory
entity44.description: A theoretical framework in which the point-like particles of particle physics are replaced by one-dimensional objects called strings.

entity45.name: gravitational waves
entity45.description: Ripples in spacetime caused by the acceleration of massive objects, such as the merger of black holes.

entity46.name: LIGO observatory
entity46.description: A facility designed to detect gravitational waves using laser interferometry.

entity55.name: quantum gravity
entity55.description: A theoretical framework that attempts to unify quantum mechanics and general relativity to describe gravity at the quantum level.

entity57.name: Hawking radiation
entity57.description: A theoretical phenomenon where black holes emit radiation due to quantum effects near the event horizon, predicted by Stephen Hawking.

entity58.name: Stephen Hawking
entity58.description: A renowned physicist who proposed the theory of Hawking radiation in 1974.;;;Refers to Stephen Hawking, the theoretical physicist known for his work on black holes and cosmology.

entity59.description: The year in which Stephen Hawking predicted the phenomenon of Hawking radiation.

entity64.name: quantum effects
entity64.description: Phenomena that occur at the quantum level, often involving particles and energy behaving in ways that classical physics cannot explain.

entity67.name: Radiation
entity67.description: The emission or transmission of energy in the form of waves or particles through space or a material medium.
